name: wingbox
description: A map of your codebase for coding agents: what a change touches, where a symbol is used.

interface.longDescription: Give your coding agent a map of your codebase. 2-4x cheaper, no missed files. Wingbox builds a graph of the repository you work in and answers from it before the agent reads source files: what a change will break, two hops away and across packages (blast radius); who uses a file, function or type; where a feature is implemented; which modules and packages depend on each other and which dependencies cross an architecture layer; and which three or four files to read first. Use it before a refactor or a cross-package change. It parses Python, TypeScript and TSX, Rust, C#, Java, Go, Ruby and Ruby on Rails with tree-sitter, and writes an offline HTML map of the repository. Everything runs on your computer with the open-source wingbox command (MIT, on PyPI): no code, graph or question is sent anywhere. The plugin needs a local shell and the command, installed once with pipx install wingbox.
defaultPrompt: In this monorepo, what will break if I change this package?
Who uses this file, and which files should I read before changing it?
Where is authentication implemented, and which modules depend on it?
